chunk_findings.detail: The `locks` view wires the concrete git probe implementation directly in the API surface: `probes=GitProbes(repo) ...` imports `GitProbes` from `ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py` and constructs it there. Under [r-adapters], git is an external dependency that must be reached through a port in `ddflow/adapters`; introducing/using a git probe implementation outside that adapter port couples the API to the concrete git implementation and prevents a fake git probe from being injected through the normal port boundary.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/metrics.py:43

chunk_findings.detail: The new `Probes` protocol and its default `GitProbes` implementation form the git port for this feature, but they live in `ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py` instead of `ddflow/adapters`. [r-adapters] requires every external dependency (explicitly including git) to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, with one implementation per function. As written, the git seam and its default adapter are service-local, so changing or swapping the external git behavior touches the service module rather than the adapter layer, violating the recorded rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py:Probes

chunk_findings.detail: `_declared` decides whether an item is in scope by looking only at `ctx.facts.landings[item][0].at`, while `_merges` filters every landing with `ctx.in_scope(i, m.at)`. Given a window where `ctx.in_scope(item, t)` is true only for `t >= 100`, and `ctx.facts.landings["A"] = [Landing(at=50, ...), Landing(at=150, ...)]`, `_merges` counts the 150 merge, but `_declared` sees the first landing at 50, treats the item as out of scope, and skips it entirely. The declared-item count and both declared shares then omit a merged item that is in scope, and if landing order is not guaranteed the result is order-dependent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/locks.py:_declared

chunk_findings.detail: This change adds the git probe port/implementation (`Probes`, `GitProbes`) under `ddflow/services/metrics` and consumes it in `locks.py` via `from .lockgit import Probes`, rather than placing the port/default adapter in `ddflow/adapters`. That violates the project's adapter guidance [r-adapters], which requires external dependencies such as git to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters` so that swapping or faking git touches one place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py:GitProbes

chunk_findings.detail: The new lock metrics view imports `Probes` from `ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py` and dispatches `view == "locks"` through it, while `lockgit.py` also provides `GitProbes` (a git-backed implementation). This places a new external-dependency port/adapter outside `ddflow/adapters`, so `ddflow metrics locks` couples the metrics service directly to a service-local git probe rather than to an adapter-layer port/fake, violating [r-adapters].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/service.py:17

chunk_findings.detail: The test file introduces a direct external dependency on the `git` binary by calling `subprocess.run(["git", ...])` in `_git` and then using it to build a real repository in `test_git_probes_read_files_and_conflicts_through_infra_git` (line 185 also imports `GitProbes` from `ddflow.services.metrics.lockgit`, not from a fake adapter). This violates [r-adapters], which requires external dependencies to go through an adapter/port and tests to use fakes rather than subprocesses. Concrete failure: on a machine where the user's global git config sets `commit.gpgsign=true` (or where `git` is not installed), `_git(tmp_path, "commit", "-qm", "base")` at line 189 raises `CalledProcessError` or `FileNotFoundError`, so the test fails even though the ddflow metrics logic under test has not changed. The test should exercise the git port with a fake, or at minimum isolate git configuration and skip when git is unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lock_metrics.py:174

chunk_findings.detail: The new `GitProbes` reaches the git subprocess through `ddflow.infra.git` (`G.paths` at line 29 and `G.run` at line 35) instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`. Git is explicitly listed in [r-adapters] as an external dependency that must have one adapter implementation under `ddflow/adapters`, so a fake or swap would touch only the adapter. Direct use of `infra.git` ties this service to the real subprocess and violates that advisory.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py:15

chunk_findings.detail: `_declared` decides whether an item is in scope by looking only at `ctx.facts.landings[item][0].at`, the first landing in that item's list. `_merges` in this same module filters and sorts every landing with `ctx.in_scope(i, m.at)`, so out-of-scope landings can exist. If item X has an out-of-scope landing first and a later in-scope landing, `_declared` skips X entirely; meanwhile `_actual` includes all landings without any `in_scope` filter, so out-of-window files can also pollute the declared-vs-written shares.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/locks.py:_declared

chunk_findings.detail: `_declared_of` returns `first.globs` for the first lease of an item and is used both by `_declared` and by `_blockers` for wait classification. If an item has multiple leases with different declared globs, e.g. Lease1 globs=("docs/a.md") and Lease2 globs=("src/b.py"), Lease2's `src/b.py` write is measured as outside Lease1's declared globs, and `_blockers` finds blockers for Lease2 using Lease1's globs. The doc says declared is "how much of a lease's globs" never touched, so the globs must come from the lease attached to that landing/wait, not the first lease ever recorded for the item.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/locks.py:_declared_of

chunk_findings.detail: `new = "\"locks.mode\""` sets the default value to the TOML string `"locks.mode"` including two double-quote characters. The intended default for `metrics.lock_revert_key` is almost certainly the config key `locks.mode` without surrounding quotes. When this knob is applied, the lock metrics report will look up the key `"locks.mode"` (with quotes) instead of `locks.mode`, so the strict-locking switch-back call described in `metrics.md` will not match the real config entry and the report will be wrong under default settings.

chunk_findings.detail: The `locks` view hard-wires the concrete git adapter `GitProbes` from `ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py` in the public API (`probes=GitProbes(repo) if view == "locks" else None`). The recorded adapter rule [r-adapters] requires external dependencies such as git to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters` so call sites and tests can substitute a fake. Given a call like `ddflow.api.metrics.view(repo, view="locks")` in a test or an environment without a usable git repository, this path instantiates the real git probe instead of an injected fake and can invoke real git subprocesses; the API should depend on an adapter/port from the adapters layer rather than importing and constructing `GitProbes` directly.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/metrics.py:14

chunk_findings.detail: `_actual` builds the file set for an item from every landing with `before`/`after`, without applying `ctx.in_scope`. For a `--since` report, this contaminates both false-serialization and declared metrics with out-of-window merges. Example: report window starts at 150; item `X` has an out-of-scope landing at 100 that changed `old.py` and an in-scope landing at 200 that changed `src/new.py`. `_declared` accepts `X` because the 200 landing is in scope, but `_actual` returns `{old.py, src/new.py}`. With declared globs `("src/new.py",)`, `actual_outside_declared_share` becomes 0.5 and `items_with_undeclared_writes` becomes 1, even though the in-scope merge wrote only the declared file. The same missing scope filter can also make a wait fail false-serialization classification because an out-of-scope blocker file overlaps the waiter.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/locks.py:_actual

chunk_findings.detail: The git dependency is introduced through `ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py` (`Probes`/`GitProbes` per the manifest) and consumed directly by `locks.py`, rather than through a port in `ddflow/adapters` as required by [r-adapters]. This places a new external-service port and its default implementation outside the adapter layer the project guidance designates for git access.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/locks.py (import of `.lockgit.Probes`) [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: The change introduces the git-probe abstraction outside the mandated adapter layer: `service.py` imports `Probes` from `.lockgit`, and the manifest says the new `ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py` adds `GitProbes` (the git implementation) along with `files`/`conflicts`. Under [r-adapters], external dependencies such as git must go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, with the implementation in that adapter. As written, the locks view depends on a git port/implementation living in `services/metrics`, so swapping or faking the git dependency requires touching service-side lock code rather than replacing the adapter port.

chunk_findings.detail: The default for `metrics.lock_revert_key` is encoded as a TOML string containing literal double quotes, `"locks.mode"`, rather than the dotted config key `locks.mode`. Any consumer that uses this knob as the key in the advertised switch-back call will target the invalid key `"locks.mode"` instead of `locks.mode`, so the reported revert-to-strict-locking action can fail to change the intended setting.

chunk_findings.detail: The new git test and its `_git` helper invoke the real `git` binary through `subprocess.run` and rely on the ambient git environment. That violates the project's [r-adapters] guidance that external dependencies go through a port and that tests use a fake instead of subprocesses. Concretely, if the test suite is run in an environment without a `git` executable (or with a global `core.hooksPath`/`GIT_DIR` that makes commits fail), `_git` raises `FileNotFoundError`/`CalledProcessError` before `GitProbes` is exercised, so the test is environment-dependent rather than a unit test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lock_metrics.py:test_git_probes_read_files_and_conflicts_through_infra_git

chunk_findings.detail: The new `locks` path constructs the concrete git probe via `GitProbes(repo)`. The added knob documentation in this diff states the probe replays merges through `git merge-tree --write-tree`, so this is an external git dependency. [r-adapters] requires every external dependency such as git to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters` so it can have one implementation and be faked in tests. Here the API imports `GitProbes` from `ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit` and instantiates it directly, so the git dependency is not behind that adapter port and the metrics API is coupled to the concrete probe implementation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/metrics.py:14,43

chunk_findings.detail: `conflicts()` cannot ever report a real textual conflict. For a conflict, `git merge-tree --write-tree` exits 1 and does not print a bare 40/64 hex result tree id (there is no result tree for a conflicted merge); the first line is conflict-report text such as a `CONFLICT`/stage line. The guard at lines 42-44 discards that output and returns `None`. So given `base` and `head` with conflicting edits, the method reports “cannot tell” instead of `True`, which the caller counts as unavailable and never as a conflict.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py:35-45

chunk_findings.detail: The new `GitProbes` calls the external `git` dependency directly through `from ...infra import git as G` and `G.paths`/`G.run` at lines 32 and 38. r-adapters requires external dependencies such as git to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters` with one implementation per function; this file introduces the port under `services/metrics` and binds it to `infra.git` instead.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py:14 [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: `_actual` unions every file ever changed by any merge of an item (`frozenset(f for p in parts for f in p or ())`), and `_waits` uses that item-wide union as `mine`/`theirs`. Files from unrelated earlier or later leases therefore count against a wait. Example: items `app` and `lib` both declare `**`; an old `app` merge and an old `lib` merge both touched `common.txt`; later a blocked `app` lease changes only `app/a.py` while the live blocking `lib` lease changes only `lib/b.py`. The current changes are disjoint, so this wait should be false serialization, but `mine.isdisjoint(theirs)` is False because both historical unions contain `common.txt`, undercounting `false_serialization`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/locks.py:_actual, used by _waits

chunk_findings.detail: The `new` value is written as `"\"strict\""`, which TOML parses as the literal string `"strict"` (including surrounding double-quote characters). Files are then scored against any declared glob from any lease in the window, not against the lease held at the merge that produced the file. Concrete failure: item A has merge M1 under lease `src/*.py` changing `src/a.py`, then a later merge M2 under lease `docs/*.md` changing `src/c.py`. The union is `{"docs/*.md", "src/*.py"}`, so `src/c.py` matches the earlier `src/*.py` glob and `actual_outside_declared_share` is reported as 0.0, even though M2's own declared globs were only `docs/*.md`. The metric undercounts false declared-glob writes; it must score each actual file against the declarations of the merge that changed it.
